title: Adaptive gamma calibration & throughput sweep for FP8/INT8 under long-context batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Validate throughput and latency behavior of FP8 and INT8 quantized model builds when serving long-context workloads with realistic batching and KV-cache warmup patterns, while ensuring calibration (per-layer gamma scaling) preserves downstream task accuracy within defined tolerances.

Hypothesis: An adaptive gamma calibration schedule that scales per-layer clipping factors using streaming representative traces will reduce accuracy regressions versus static calibration while enabling more aggressive quantization profiles that improve throughput by 10-35% depending on batch coalescing and sequence lengths.

Acceptance criteria:
- Baseline: float32 run (runtime-1.20) p50/p95/p99 latency and throughput for target model (redwood/gptx-7b) across sequence lengths [512, 2k, 8k] with batching factors [1, 4, 16].
- Quantized variants (FP8, INT8, hybrid FP8+INT8) should:
  1) not exceed +2% task-level metric degradation for QA EM or summarization ROUGE-L compared to baseline after calibration;
  2) show stable p99 tail (<= +12% relative to baseline) at production batching;
  3) provide >= 10% throughput improvement at median traffic profiles.
- Calibration artifacts, scripts, and evaluation notebooks checked into repo with reproducible runbook.
notes_on_methodology: We will use a micro-benchmark harness that replays representative streaming traces with realistic inter-arrival times to emulate prefix and KV warmup. Metrics collected: token throughput (tokens/s), request throughput (req/s), latency p50/p95/p99, memory high-water, kernel fallback counts, KL divergence per-layer of logits, token-level perplexity delta, and task-level EM/F1/ROUGE. Calibration: adaptive gamma optimizer that updates per-layer clipping thresholds using streaming quantization statistics (activations histograms, outlier detection). All runs include cold, warm, and steady-state phases; warmup period defined as first 200 tokens per sequence. Batch coalescing simulated with mix of microbursts and steady traffic to surface interaction effects.

implementation_plan: 1) Stabilize harness and reproduce baseline float32 numbers. 2) Run static FP8/INT8 calibration (existing pipeline) to create comparison points. 3) Run adaptive gamma calibration across representative traces, produce calibrated checkpoints. 4) Execute sweep matrix: sequences [512,2k,8k] x batches [1,4,16] x traffic profiles [steady,microburst] x quant variants [FP8,INT8,hybrid]. 5) Collect metrics, analyze regressions, iterate on gamma schedule and batch coalescer/backoff. 6) Document runbook and merge calibrated artifacts to release branch.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: aggressive per-layer clipping may introduce systematic bias in early attention layers causing task-level degradation. Mitigation: add per-layer rollback thresholds and quick A/B canary with automatic fallback to float or less-aggressive quant for routes with high regression. Risk: kernel fallback spikes under memory pressure. Mitigation: implement memory headroom guard and conservative kernel set as fallback policy.
next_steps: Tune coalescing window and add memory headroom guard by 2026-03-15. Schedule canary runs on Dedicated pool with reduced traffic to validate p99 tail. Prepare PR with calibrated checkpoints and evaluation notebooks for review.
observability_checks: Ensure tracing annotated with quant variant tag, gamma schedule id, calibration seed, and kernel-fallback counters. Add dashboard panels: per-route token throughput, p99 delta vs baseline, per-layer KL heatmap over time.
qa_plan: Run end-to-end QA with 3 canonical tasks (QA EM, summarization ROUGE-L, dialogue coherence) using held-out production-like datasets. Acceptance requires passing predefined thresholds and manual sanity checks on hallucination metrics. All QA runs reproducible via bench harness scripts in repo.
